question: Does the rhythm in the published lower-limb surface EMG amplitude summaries estimate the rhythm in the exported knee flexion angles of the same trial?
design: Retrospective comparison of whole-trial rhythms on different devices, paired by source participant identifier and speed only. One 0.5 m/s trial per person; no row alignment, EEG, force plate or time-of-onset comparison. Distinct from the future joint-angle model. Same held subset already studied for joint-angle error; their muscle rhythm and this new reference outcome were not used in choosing this protocol.
selection: Use IDs 1 through 40 for estimating the median reference rhythm and training a fixed affine adjustment; use 41 through 52 once for evaluation. Exclude any participant missing either original file or failing the fixed checks. Do not use IDs 53–59; do not read person metadata. If two original EMG or kinematic files have the same bytes among selected eligible people, keep earliest training occurrence, remove overlapping evaluation occurrences, and keep at most one evaluation occurrence per unique file. Report missing/duplicate reasons without replacements.
signals: Average normalized spectral power from all twelve finite EMG amplitude channels, with an independent timestamp for each published row in milliseconds; retain their original recorded order. Independently extract bilateral knee flexion/extension values from the Xsens ZXY export on its 60 Hz frame clock, computing one normalized spectrum for each knee. Unilateral dominant cycles per minute (not a measured step count).
spectral: Use 5 <= time from the first available row < 45 seconds separately in each device. Require >=45 seconds span, increasing timestamps, contiguous kinematic frames, EMG gaps no larger than 110 ms, at least 500 EMG and 2000 joint samples in the window. On fixed grid 0.45 to 1.50 Hz inclusive with 0.0025 Hz increment, demean each channel, multiply by a Hann time taper defined over the 40-second interval and project directly onto the complex oscillator at actual timestamps. Normalize each channel spectrum by its summed in-band power, then average channels. Dominant rate uses the earliest maximum. Require finite channels and nonzero band power. Do not change band to suppress an observed harmonic. Neither physiological step counts nor EMG onset inferred.
estimators: 1. Mean absolute error for assigning every test person the training median IMU rhythm. 2. Direct EMG dominant rate in cycles/minute (60 times Hz). 3. Train ordinary least-squares target = a + b*EMG on eligible training participants; freeze coefficients before reading paired held-out EMG/rate outcomes. No other features, tuning or retraining. 4. Matched wrong-person diagnostic cyclically reassigning raw test EMG rhythmic rates by ascending participant ID, wrapping once (never used as a deployable predictor).
criteria: Primary success of a useful pair is direct EMG beating both the training-median reference and the wrong-person assignment on mean absolute error and in strictly more than half the test subjects versus each. Always report all outcomes, signed bias, number of participants, per-person differences, and leave-one-person-out range of the mean paired difference. Report the trained affine estimator separately, without selecting it after seeing the test results.
public: Publish analysis and aggregate or pseudonymous per-record rhythm estimates/errors, never raw EEG, EMG, personal demographics, device free-text or conversation histories. Clearly distinguish a dominant periodicity from a validated gait-event counter and timing across devices.
